investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-07T12:30–12:38Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods stuck unscheduled for 126–145 seconds until the eval timed out. Because the agent pod never started, the runner could not collect any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885, createAgent call with machineType "remote") never receives a running pod, so it cannot populate the required evidence fields (vmIdPresent, remoteState) mandated by the contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=131719 (~131s) — the probe ran for over two minutes before failing, consistent with a scheduling timeout rather than an immediate API error.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 nodes that do not carry kata.peerpods.io/vm may have had their labels changed or the pod spec's affinity rules may have become overly restrictive, reducing the schedulable node pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity pressure.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm support (2 of 6) may be insufficient for the concurrent load of eval probes plus production workloads, causing transient exhaustion during peak usage.

QUATERNARY — a stuck or leaked remote-agent VM from a previous eval run that was not cleaned up, holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and preventing new scheduling; the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to prevent this but a prior crash could bypass cleanup.

investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was last written approximately 659 minutes before the eval ran at 2026-08-07T12:38:10.255Z, meaning the workflow missed at least two expected refresh cycles. The eval contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482) asserts snapshotAgeMinutes max 300; the live evidence value of 659 directly violated this assertion. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-07T12:30–12:38Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods stuck unscheduled for 126–145 seconds until the eval timed out. Because the agent pod never started, the runner could not collect any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885, createAgent call with machineType "remote") never receives a running pod, so it cannot populate the required evidence fields (vmIdPresent, remoteState) mandated by the contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259.

Add a separate eval assertion that alerts when snapshotAgeMinutes exceeds the staleAfterMinutes registry value (360) in addition to the contract max (300), to distinguish a warning-level staleness from a hard contract violation.

Add a historical trend eval that tracks snapshotAgeMinutes across consecutive runs to detect gradual drift (e.g., a workflow running less frequently than scheduled) before it crosses the hard threshold.

Consider adding an eval that validates the GitHub Pages deployment status for the observability snapshot artifact independently of the snapshot content age, to distinguish a deployment failure from a workflow execution failure.
